summary: The Kokkos RNG pool is seeded in the constructor's member-initializer list from `seed`, which is an uninitialized PairBrownian member at that point (it is only parsed in settings()), so the user's seed is ignored and an indeterminate value is used.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_brownian_kokkos.cpp:49-51:
  PairBrownianKokkos<DeviceType>::PairBrownianKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : PairBrownian(lmp),
                                                                    rand_pool(seed + comm->me)
src/COLLOID/pair_brownian.cpp:46-51 -- the base constructor sets only `single_enable` and `random`; it never initializes `seed` (declared as a bare `int seed;` at src/COLLOID/pair_brownian.h:51).  `seed` is first assigned in PairBrownian::settings (src/COLLOID/pair_brownian.cpp:368), which runs AFTER the constructor.  grep shows `rand_pool` is never re-initialized: the only other uses in the file are get_state() (:278) and free_state() (:476).
Every other KOKKOS PAIR style with an RNG re-initializes the pool in init_style() once seed is known, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:83-90 `rand_pool = decltype(rand_pool)(seed + comm->me, unique_token.size());` (the fix styles can use the member-init list because Fix constructors parse the seed in the base constructor).
failure_scenario: `pair_style brownian/kk mu 1 1 rin rout T 5813` -- the 5813 seed never reaches the device RNG; the stream is whatever the uninitialized memory held, so runs are not reproducible and changing the seed changes nothing. Reading the indeterminate int is also UB.
suggested_fix: Default-construct rand_pool and (re)initialize it in init_style() after PairBrownian::init_style(), e.g. `rand_pool = decltype(rand_pool)(seed + comm->me, unique_token.size());`, mirroring pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:83-90.

summary: compute() calls ev_init(eflag,vflag,0) (alloc = 0) but the style never allocates eatom/k_eatom, so with eflag_atom set `Pair::eatom` stays nullptr and compute pe/atom dereferences a null pointer.
failure_scenario: `pair_style brownian/kk ...` plus `compute 1 all pe/atom` (or any dump/compute that sets ENERGY_ATOM) -> segmentation fault on the first invocation of the compute.
suggested_fix: Either call `ev_init(eflag,vflag)` (alloc = 1) so the base allocates and zeroes eatom, or add a k_eatom dual view allocated under `if (eflag_atom)` like every other KOKKOS pair style.

summary: With neighflag FULL the kernel never applies the equal-and-opposite force/torque to atom j, so each pair is evaluated twice with INDEPENDENT random numbers and the stochastic pair force is no longer antisymmetric -- momentum is not conserved; the DPD KOKKOS styles reject FULL for exactly this reason.
failure_scenario: `package kokkos neigh full` (which forces newton off, kokkos.cpp:857-860) with `pair_style brownian/kk`: total linear momentum random-walks away instead of being conserved, and the pair virial is built from two different random forces for the same pair.
suggested_fix: Reject FULL (and newton off) in PairBrownianKokkos::init_style() with an explicit error, as pair_dpd_ext_kokkos does, or drop FULL from EnabledNeighFlags.

summary: rand_pool is seeded in the constructor member-initializer list from PairBrownian::seed, which is only assigned later in settings(); the user seed is ignored and an indeterminate value is used. init_style() never re-initializes the pool.
verified_by: orchestrator (ctor at :49-51, init_style at :80-82 does not touch rand_pool; contrast the correct idiom in pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:129/134 and pair_dpd_ext_tstat_kokkos.cpp:83/88 which init the pool in init_style once seed is known).

summary: compute() calls ev_init(eflag,vflag,0) and only ever allocates k_vatom, so with eflag_atom set Pair::eatom stays nullptr while ev_setup still raises maxeatom; compute pe/atom then dereferences it unguarded.
verified_by: orchestrator (Pair::ev_setup src/pair.cpp:989-995 skips the allocation when alloc==0; src/compute_pe_atom.cpp:131-133 reads force->pair->eatom without a null check; pair_brownian_kokkos.cpp allocates only k_vatom at :165-167, whereas e.g. pair_dpd_ext_tstat_kokkos.cpp:124-130 allocates eatom itself).

summary: The per-element weight read from wjelem is stored in an int instead of a double, truncating any non-integer element weight (and zeroing weights below 1) in both the descriptor and the descriptor-derivative kernels.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:757-758 'const int jelem = t_jelems[ipair]; int weight = t_wjelem[jelem];' (MLIAPSO3SpectrumTag), and the same 'int weight = t_wjelem[jelem];' at lines 893 and 933 (MLIAPSO3SpectrumDXDRTag). t_wjelem is 'float_1d t_wjelem' (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.h:75), filled from the double array descriptor->wjelem in src/KOKKOS/mliap_descriptor_kokkos.h:36-40. The CPU original declares it double: src/ML-IAP/mliap_so3.cpp:819 'double weight;' with 'weight = wjelem[jelem];' at line 871 (and 952/1005/1063 for spectrum_dxdr), used as 'm_clist_r[tn] = m_clist_r[tn] * weight;' (line 914). The value comes straight from the 'welems' line of the SO3 parameter file, parsed with utils::numeric (src/ML-IAP/mliap_descriptor_so3.cpp:150-155), so it is an arbitrary real number.
failure_scenario: An SO3 parameter file with 'welems 1.0 0.5' (or any non-integer weight): with pair_style mliap/kk the second element's contribution is multiplied by 0 instead of 0.5, so all descriptors, energies and forces involving that element are wrong, while pair_style mliap gives the correct answer. Even 'welems 1.0 1.0' is only correct by luck.
suggested_fix: Change 'int weight' to 'double weight' at lines 758, 893 and 933 (the later 'double(weight)' casts then become no-ops).

summary: spectrum_dxdr() grows m_ulist_r/m_ulist_i/m_dYlm_r/m_dYlm_i for a larger atom count but forgets m_dclist, which the same kernel subviews by the identical chunk index.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:807-820 re-creates m_clisttot_r/i, and inside 'if (delta > 0)' re-creates m_ulist_r, m_ulist_i, m_dYlm_r and m_dYlm_i with the new num_of_temp -- m_dclist is absent. The only place m_dclist is allocated is init_arrays (line 244 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(m_dclist, num_of_temp, m_nmax, m_numYlms, 3, ...)'), which is called only from spectrum() (line 679). The DXDR kernel indexes it with the same chunk index as the views that were grown: line 886 'auto dclist = Kokkos::subview(m_dclist,ii_chunk,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL);' with 'int ii_chunk = ii%m_chunk_size;' (line 879). spectrum() is skipped whenever the model is linear and eflag is 0 -- src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:113 'if (model->nonlinearflag || eflag)' and MLIAPModelLinear leaves nonlinearflag = 0 (src/ML-IAP/mliap_model.cpp:39).
failure_scenario: pair_style mliap/kk model linear ... descriptor so3 ...: on a non-thermo timestep (eflag = 0) where list->inum has grown since the last energy step, spectrum_dxdr enlarges m_ulist_r but not m_dclist, and the kernel writes dclist(n,i,k) through a subview whose first index is past the end of m_dclist -- out-of-bounds device writes and corrupted forces (or an abort with Kokkos bounds checking).
suggested_fix: Re-create m_dclist alongside m_ulist_r/m_dYlm_* in the 'if (delta > 0)' block of spectrum_dxdr, or simply call init_arrays(nlocal, ncoefs) at the top of spectrum_dxdr the way spectrum() does.

summary: The growth test for the 3-D k_dplist_r view compares the total element count against only its first extent, so the view is destroyed and reallocated on essentially every spectrum() call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:697-701 'totali = (bigint) totaln * ncoefs * 3; if ( totali > (bigint)k_dplist_r.extent(0)) { memoryKK->realloc_kokkos(k_dplist_r, "MLIAP_SO3Kokkos:m_dplist_r", (int)totaln, ncoefs, 3); ... }'. k_dplist_r is 'float_3d' (npairs x ncoefs x 3), so extent(0) is totaln, and the test is 'totaln*ncoefs*3 > totaln_prev', which is true for every realistic ncoefs. The neighbouring tests for the 1-D m_sbes_array (line 684) and m_rip_array (line 691) correctly compare against the flat length.
failure_scenario: Every timestep that computes descriptors frees and re-allocates a npairs*ncoefs*3 double device array, adding an avoidable large allocation/deallocation per step.
suggested_fix: Compare against the actual first extent, e.g. 'if (totaln > (int)k_dplist_r.extent(0) || ncoefs != (int)k_dplist_r.extent(1))'.

summary: Pair-major offsets into the spherical-Bessel and radial-integral arrays are computed in int in three kernels, while the arrays themselves are sized with bigint and the CPU original uses bigint indices.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:581,597 'int ipair = t_ij(ii); ... const int gindex = (ipair - 1) * findex;' (findex = m_Nmax*(m_lmax+1)), line 777 'int gindex = (ipair - 1) * findex;', and lines 659-667 '(ipair - 1) * m_Nmax * (m_lmax + 1) + (bigint) i * (m_lmax + 1) + l' / '(ipair - 1) * m_nmax * (m_lmax + 1) + ...' -- all int products. The CPU version keeps these in bigint: src/ML-IAP/mliap_so3.cpp:703-704 'bigint ipair = 0; bigint gindex;', line 722 'gindex = (ipair - 1) * findex;', lines 795-803. The allocation side already uses bigint (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:683 'totali = (bigint) totaln * m_Nmax * (m_lmax + 1);'), and the sibling DXDR kernel gets it right at line 912 'bigint gindex = (bigint) (ipair - 1) * findex;', so this is an internal inconsistency.
failure_scenario: npairs * m_Nmax * (lmax+1) above 2^31 wraps to a negative offset and the kernel reads/writes far outside m_sbes_array/m_rip_array. Note the arrays would then be tens of GB, so this is only reachable on very large unified-memory nodes; it is nevertheless a latent 32-bit truncation the CPU code explicitly avoids.
suggested_fix: Declare ipair/gindex as bigint in the MLIAPSO3GetSBESArrayTag, MLIAPSO3GetRipArrayTag and MLIAPSO3SpectrumTag operators, matching line 912.

summary: m_chunk_size is never initialized in the constructor and is only set by init_arrays(), which spectrum_dxdr() does not call, so a first call to spectrum_dxdr() without a preceding spectrum() takes a modulus by an indeterminate value.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.h:84 declares 'int m_chunk_size;' with no initializer and the constructor (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:39-55) initializes m_rcut, m_alpha, m_lmax, m_nmax, m_Nmax, m_numYlms, m_init_arrays, m_dfac_l1/l2, m_pfac_l1/l2, m_idxu_count, m_idxy_count and alloc_* but not m_chunk_size. It is assigned only in init_arrays (line 223), which is called only from spectrum() (line 679). spectrum_dxdr() uses it at line 810 ('std::min(nlocal, m_chunk_size)') and its kernel at line 879 ('int ii_chunk = ii%m_chunk_size;') and line 859 ('start += m_chunk_size').
failure_scenario: If compute_forces() ever runs before compute_descriptors() (a linear model on a step with eflag = 0, see pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:113), the chunk loop divides by an indeterminate int -- integer division by zero on the device, or an arbitrary chunk index. In practice the setup step always has eflag = 1, so the field is set before it matters, but nothing enforces that.
suggested_fix: Initialize m_chunk_size in the constructor (and ideally call init_arrays() at the top of spectrum_dxdr() as spectrum() does).

summary: The per-element weight is read into an 'int' (also at :893 and :933) although wjelem is a double array, truncating any non-integer element weight and zeroing weights below 1 in both the descriptor and its derivative.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:758/:893/:933 'int weight = t_wjelem[jelem];' vs src/ML-IAP/mliap_so3.cpp:819 and :952 'double weight;').
orchestrator (read code directly; found by rules_D)
summary: NPair style halffull/newton/tri/trim/skip/kk/device is registered with the orthogonal class NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTrimDevice (TRI=0) although its mask carries NP_TRI and the triclinic alias NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice declared on line 219 is left unused.
evidence: npair_halffull_kokkos.h:219-223 vs the host sibling at 225-229 (which correctly uses NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimHost) and the non-skip triclinic entry at 207-211. npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:112-129 uses TRI to select the delta-based comparison that is required for triclinic ghost coordinates.
failure_scenario: Triclinic box, newton on, a pair style needing a trimmed half-from-full list plus a skip list (e.g. pair hybrid sub-style) on a GPU: exact-coordinate tie-breaking on epsilon-shifted ghost coordinates double-counts or drops pairs -> wrong forces/energies.
suggested_fix: Use NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice on line 221. Also rename the mislabeled orthogonal ghost entry at line 262 (halffull/newton/tri/trim/ghost/kk/device -> halffull/newton/trim/ghost/kk/device), which duplicates the key of the real triclinic entry at 288 (cosmetic: selection is by mask).

summary: NPair style halffull/newton/tri/trim/skip/kk/device is registered with the NON-triclinic class NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTrimDevice (TRI=0) instead of the triclinic NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice (TRI=1) declared on the line right above it.
failure_scenario: KOKKOS device run in a triclinic box (e.g. 'change_box all triclinic' or a restart with tilt) with newton on, a pair style that needs a half list built from a full list (halffull), a trimmed sub-cutoff request and a skip list (hybrid pair style / subset neighbor request).  The TRI=0 exact-coordinate branch is used for local/ghost pairs, so epsilon-level coordinate shifts introduced by the orthog->lambda->orthog transform make some i/j ghost pairs be counted twice and others dropped -> silently wrong forces/energies, non-reproducible between runs.
suggested_fix: Change line 221 to name NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice (matching the alias on line 219 and the host entry on line 227).

summary: NPair style key on line 262 is misspelled 'halffull/newton/tri/trim/ghost/kk/device' for an ORTHOGONAL (TRI=0, no NP_TRI) entry, duplicating the key of the genuine triclinic entry on line 288.
failure_scenario: An orthogonal-box KOKKOS device run using a trimmed halffull ghost list prints 'pair build: halffull/newton/tri/trim/ghost/kk/device' in the neighbor list info, telling the user a triclinic build style is in use when it is not -- and makes the two entries indistinguishable when debugging.
suggested_fix: Rename the key on line 262 to halffull/newton/trim/ghost/kk/device to match its host sibling on line 268 and its NP_ORTHO-only mask.

summary: KOKKOS npair style keys order their name tokens differently from the CPU npair styles they mirror, so 40 KOKKOS npair keys have no identically named CPU counterpart and the 'pair build:' info line is not comparable between a CPU and a KOKKOS run.
evidence:
Token order differs systematically (KOKKOS first, CPU second):
  half/bin/newtoff/size/kk/*   (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:102)  vs  half/size/bin/newtoff  (src/npair_bin.h:44)
  half/bin/newton/size/kk/*    (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:97)   vs  half/size/bin/newton   (src/npair_bin.h:49)
  half/bin/newtoff/ghost/kk/*  (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:82)   vs  half/bin/ghost/newtoff (src/npair_bin_ghost.h:22)
  halffull/newton/trim/kk/*    (src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.h)  vs  halffull/trim/newton (src/npair_halffull.h:89)
  halffull/newton/tri/trim/kk/*                                  vs  halffull/trim/newton/tri (src/npair_halffull.h:95)
  skip/trim/ghost/kk/*         (src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.h)  vs  skip/ghost/trim        (src/npair_skip.h:45)
Full list of the 40 affected keys in progress_rules_D/rule4d.json.  This is cosmetic rather than functional because NPair styles are internal: Neighbor::choose_pair() selects by bitmask, and the registered name is only used for the 'pair build:' line printed by Neighbor (src/neighbor.cpp:1952).
failure_scenario: A developer diffing the neighbor-list info block of a CPU run against a KOKKOS run (a standard way to check that -suffix kk selected an equivalent build style) sees names that do not correspond and cannot tell whether the same request was satisfied; grep-based tooling keyed on the CPU names finds no KOKKOS match.
suggested_fix: Rename the KOKKOS npair keys to the CPU token order (half/size/bin/newtoff, halffull/trim/newton, skip/ghost/trim, ...) so each KOKKOS key is its CPU counterpart plus the /kk/{host,device} suffix; the masks and classes need no change.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are stored as int in NeighborKokkosExecute, truncating the half box lengths and corrupting minimum_image_check(), which decides whether special-bond scaling is applied to a pair.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:261 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' with the matching constructor parameters at :303 'const int & _xprd_half, const int & _yprd_half, const int & _zprd_half'.  They are initialized in src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:206 from 'domain->xprd_half,domain->yprd_half,domain->zprd_half', which are declared 'double xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' in src/domain.h:50.  They are then used in floating point comparisons: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:420-425 'if (xperiodic && fabs(dx) > xprd_half) return 1;', which must match src/domain.h:198-204 exactly.
failure_scenario: Box with xprd = 9.0 -> domain->xprd_half = 4.5 but the functor stores 4.  A 1-4 special-bond partner whose |dx| is 4.2 makes minimum_image_check() return 1 on the KOKKOS path and 0 on the CPU path, so the pair is stored without the special-bond code and the special_lj/special_coul factor is never applied -> wrong energies/forces for molecular systems in small periodic boxes (and every pair in a box shorter than 2 length units, where xprd_half truncates to 0 or 1).
suggested_fix: Change the three members and the three constructor parameters to double.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are declared 'const int' in NeighborKokkosExecute (and identically in NPairSSAKokkosExecute, npair_ssa_kokkos.h:175) but are initialized from domain->xprd_half etc., which are double. The truncated values are then used in the floating-point test of minimum_image_check(), which decides whether a pair gets special-bond coding.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:261 and src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:175 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' vs src/domain.h:50 'double xprd_half, ...' and the reference test at src/domain.h:200 'if (xperiodic && fabs(dx) > xprd_half) return 1;'). In a box with a non-integer half length the KOKKOS and CPU builds disagree on which pairs carry special-bond coding.

summary: pair gran/hertz/history/kk ignores fix rigid body masses when computing the effective mass meff, silently diverging from the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:350 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass);' with imass/jmass taken straight from rmass (lines 274, 306). CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hertz_history.cpp:176-183 (identical block to pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:133-142) does 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; }' after refreshing and forward-communicating mass_rigid. No fix_rigid/mass_rigid reference exists anywhere under src/KOKKOS.
failure_scenario: 'fix rigid' + 'pair_style gran/hertz/history/kk': damping and friction use the particle mass instead of the body mass, giving different forces from the non-kk run with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port mass_rigid to a device view (fix_rigid->extract plus forward comm each reneighbor) or error out in init_style when fix_rigid is set.

summary: gran/hertz/history/kk stores special_bonds lj factors in the base class int special_lj[4], truncating fractional factors to 0/1.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:142-145 'special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...' assigns doubles into src/pair.h:247 'int special_lj[4];'; the /kk header src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.h:66-104 declares no KK_FLOAT shadow. Kernel: line 297 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]);', line 300 'if (factor_lj == 0) continue;'. CPU uses the true doubles (src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hertz_history.cpp, 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;').
failure_scenario: 'special_bonds lj 0.5 1 1' with gran/hertz/history/kk drops the 1-2 contacts entirely instead of scaling them by 0.5.
suggested_fix: Add 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' to the KOKKOS granular pair style headers, or widen Pair::special_lj to double.

summary: PairHybridScaledKokkos::settings() drops the CPU guard that rejects INTEL/GPU/OMP accelerator sub-styles, so hybrid/scaled/kk silently accepts sub-styles whose force accumulation is incompatible with its clear/scale/restore scheme.
evidence: diff of the two settings() bodies shows the /kk copy is missing src/pair_hybrid_scaled.cpp:388-391 (missing right after 'compute_tally[nstyles] = 1;' at src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:562) 'if ((styles[nstyles]->suffix_flag & (Suffix::INTEL | Suffix::GPU | Suffix::OMP)) != 0) error->all(FLERR, "Pair style hybrid/scaled does not support accelerator styles");' -- it is the only substantive difference besides the function name. The scheme in src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:340-384 zeroes atom->f/atom->torque before every sub-style and reads them back right after that sub-style's compute(), which a GPU style (whose forces are added later by FixGPU::post_force) or an OMP style with thread-private force buffers does not satisfy.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style hybrid/scaled/kk 1.0 lj/cut/gpu 10.0 0.5 coul/cut/gpu 10.0' is accepted; the GPU sub-style's forces are added in FixGPU::post_force after the hybrid already snapshotted and restored f, so the scale factors are not applied and the forces are wrong -- the CPU hybrid/scaled refuses the same input.
suggested_fix: Copy the suffix_flag check from src/pair_hybrid_scaled.cpp into PairHybridScaledKokkos::settings() (KOKKOS sub-styles are unaffected since Suffix::KOKKOS is not in the mask).

summary: single() and born_matrix() index scaleidx/atomvar with the loop counter m instead of the sub-style index map[itype][jtype][m], so the atom-style-scale branch is chosen from the wrong sub-style's data.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:654-663 'double scale = scaleval[map[itype][jtype][m]]; esum += scale * pstyle->single(...); if (scaleidx[m] < 0 || atomvar[m] < 0) { fforce += scale * fone; } else { update_atomscale(m); ... }' -- note scaleval uses map[itype][jtype][m] while scaleidx/atomvar/update_atomscale use the bare m. Same pattern at lines 738-748 in born_matrix(). (The CPU original src/pair_hybrid_scaled.cpp:263-276 has the identical mistake, so this is a faithfully copied bug rather than a KOKKOS-only one.)
failure_scenario: hybrid/scaled with more than one sub-style where the sub-style order and the per-type-pair map order differ: 'pair_write' or a tally compute that calls single() picks the wrong scale mode, applying a constant scale where an atom-style variable was meant (or the reverse, evaluating the wrong variable).
suggested_fix: Hoist 'const int ms = map[itype][jtype][m];' and use scaleval[ms], scaleidx[ms], atomvar[ms] and update_atomscale(ms) throughout both loops; fix the CPU original the same way.

summary: single()/born_matrix() call update_atomscale() which writes into the host scratch array atomscale and into k_atomscale, but both are only ever allocated inside compute().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:298-303 allocates them only under 'if (atomscaleflag && (atom->nmax > nmaxatomscale))' inside compute(); update_atomscale (lines 211-223) does 'input->variable->compute_atom(atomvar[m], igroupall, atomscale, 1, 0); auto h_atomscale = k_atomscale.view_host(); for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; ++i) h_atomscale(i) = atomscale[i];' with no allocation check, and single() (line 663) / born_matrix() (line 743) call it directly. The constructor leaves atomscale nullptr (line 37) and k_atomscale default-constructed (extent 0).
failure_scenario: 'pair_write' or a pair tally compute invoking single() on a hybrid/scaled/kk whose scale factor is an atom-style variable, before compute() has run with that variable active -> compute_atom writes through a null pointer and h_atomscale(i) writes past a zero-extent view.
suggested_fix: Move the atomscale/k_atomscale allocation into update_atomscale() (grow to atom->nmax on entry) so every caller is safe.

summary: The degenerate-geometry guards compare against SMALL*SMALL with SMALL = 1.0e-100, which underflows to 0 when KK_FLOAT is float, so the zero-length checks that the CPU style relies on become inert.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_dipole_kokkos.cpp:31 `static constexpr double SMALL = 1.0e-100;`, :154-155 `const KK_FLOAT r2 = delx*delx + dely*dely + delz*delz;` / `if (r2 < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)*static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)) return;` and :181-183 `const KK_FLOAT len2 = fx*fx + fy*fy + fz*fz;` / `if (len2 < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)*static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)) return;`. With KK_FLOAT = float (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:399-408, LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE / SINGLE_DOUBLE) static_cast<float>(1.0e-100) is 0.0f, so both tests become `< 0.0f` and never trigger. The CPU base tests the un-squared quantity in double: src/DIPOLE/angle_dipole.cpp:35 `static constexpr double SMALL = 1.0e-100;`, :94-95 `r = sqrt(...); if (r < SMALL) continue;` and :120-121 `len = sqrt(fx*fx+fy*fy+fz*fz); if (len < SMALL) continue;`.
failure_scenario: Single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, angle_style dipole/kk, with a dipole atom coincident with its reference atom (r == 0) or a dipole exactly parallel to the bond vector (delT == 0 so fx=fy=fz=0): the CPU skips the angle, the /kk kernel divides by rmu == 0 or by sqrt(len2) == 0 and writes inf/NaN into torque and f.
suggested_fix: Do the comparison in double (compare `static_cast<double>(r2) < SMALL*SMALL`) or replace 1.0e-100 with a floor representable in KK_FLOAT.

summary: compute_scalar()/compute_vector() always call the host-facing tbias->remove_bias_all()/restore_bias_all() instead of the kokkosable-guarded *_kk() variants, forcing a device->host->device round trip of v on every invocation even when the bias compute is a KOKKOS style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:52-58 and 79-84 (and 126-132, 153-158): 'atomKK->sync(tbias->execution_space, tbias->datamask_read); tbias->remove_bias_all(); atomKK->modified(...); atomKK->sync(execution_space, V_MASK);'.  For a kk bias, e.g. src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_ramp_kokkos.cpp:167-171, remove_bias_all() is 'remove_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK);' -- an unconditional full copy of v to the host.  Every other KOKKOS caller uses the guarded form, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:136 'if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();' and fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:558, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:212/371, fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:353.
failure_scenario: compute temp/sphere/kk with 'bias' pointing at a temp/ramp/kk or temp/region/kk compute on a GPU build: every thermo evaluation copies the full v array device->host and back, which is exactly the per-step transfer the KOKKOS package policy forbids. Results are still correct, only slow.
suggested_fix: Follow the package pattern: 'if (tbias->kokkosable) tbias->remove_bias_all_kk(); else { atomKK->sync(tbias->execution_space, tbias->datamask_read); tbias->remove_bias_all(); atomKK->modified(...); }' and likewise for restore.

summary: A leftover `|| 1` in the compute_X dispatch makes the condition always true, so the GPU team/scratch code path for compute_X is dead and every GPU run falls back to the serialized parallel_scan range policy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_acks2_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:343 `if (execution_space == HostKK || 1) { // CPU`. The corresponding H-matrix dispatch 40 lines above is correct: line 303 `if (execution_space == HostKK) { // CPU`, and fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:579 also uses the plain `if (execution_space == HostKK)`. Because of `|| 1` the `else` block at lines 354-376 (FixACKS2ReaxFFKokkosComputeXFunctor team launch, plus its `Kokkos::deep_copy(d_mfill_offset,0)`) can never execute.
failure_scenario: Any GPU run of `fix acks2/reaxff/kk`: compute_X is executed with `Kokkos::parallel_scan(nn, ...)` over a RangePolicy on the device, which serializes the neighbor loop per atom instead of using the team/vector kernel, giving a large slowdown on the X-matrix build. It also means compute_x_team has been shipped untested; note that if it were re-enabled it contains a race, `a_X_diag[i] -= X_val` at line 1156 is executed by all 32 vector lanes of a ThreadVectorRange with a non-atomic accessor when NEIGHFLAG==FULL.
suggested_fix: Drop the `|| 1` so the team path is used on device, and re-verify compute_x_team (in particular make the `a_X_diag[i]` update at line 1156 a per-thread accumulation or an atomic) before enabling it.

summary: The Wolf self-energy is accumulated in a host loop over atom->q[i] although only the DEVICE copy of q was synced, so a device-side sort or a device-side charge update leaves the host charges stale and the self-energy (and per-atom eatom) wrong.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_wolf_kokkos.cpp:88 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read);` (execution_space = Device for the /kk and /kk/device variants) is the only sync, then lines 119-123 `for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++) { double qisq = atom->q[i]*atom->q[i]; eng_coul += ...; }` and lines 148-152 `eatom[i] += ...` read the HOST array atom->q. src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.cpp:124-134 (sort_kokkos) sorts d_q on the device and then calls `atomKK->modified(Device, ALL_MASK & ~F_MASK)` (Q_MASK included), leaving the host mirror stale; src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:537 likewise does `atomKK->modified(execution_space,Q_MASK)`.
failure_scenario: GPU run with the default atom sorting: after AtomKokkos::sort_device() the host q array holds the pre-sort permutation, so eatom[i] gets another atom's self-energy (per-atom energies wrong); with any /kk fix that updates charges on the device (fix qeq/*) the total eng_coul self-term is computed from stale charges and the global Coulomb energy is wrong.
suggested_fix: Either add `atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK);` before the host loops (and keep the loops off the critical path), or better, compute the self-energy in a Kokkos kernel over d_q so the term stays device-resident.

summary: Leftover developer 'FIX:' comment plus redundant re-creation of the coefficient dual views in read_restart(), and per-atom memory tags mislabelled 'improper:' in bond styles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:264-267 '// FIX: Removed "DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d" to use the class members / // instead of creating local shadowed variables. / k_k = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d("BondHarmonic::k", n+1);' - BondHarmonic::read_restart (src/MOLECULE/bond_harmonic.cpp:169) already calls the virtual allocate(), i.e. BondHarmonicKokkos::allocate() (:213-228), which has just created these very views, so lines 266-270 leak/replace them for nothing (same shape in src/KOKKOS/bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:279-287). Separately, bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:77,84, bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:77,84 and bond_quartic_exp_kokkos.cpp:72,79 pass "improper:eatom"/"improper:vatom" as the memory tag inside a BOND style.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers; the stray 'FIX:' note reads as leftover scratch commentary in a stable release, and the 'improper:' tags make 'info memory' / memory-leak reports attribute bond per-atom arrays to improper styles.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'FIX:' comment and the redundant dual-view (re)construction in read_restart(), and change the memory tags to "bond:eatom"/"bond:vatom" as the other bond kokkos styles already do.

summary: Member 'neighflag_qeq_set' is declared but never initialized nor used anywhere in the source tree.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.h:29 'int neighflag_qeq_set;'; 'grep -rn neighflag_qeq_set src/' returns only this declaration. It is not set in the KokkosLMP constructor (src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:116-490, which initializes neigh_thread_set, threads_per_atom_set, pair_team_size_set, ... but not this one) and never read.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today, but the uninitialized member is a trap for anyone who later adds a 'if (neighflag_qeq_set)' test analogous to neigh_thread_set.
suggested_fix: Remove the member, or initialize it in the constructor and use it to distinguish an explicit 'neigh/qeq' setting like neigh_thread_set does.

summary: The Kokkos random pool is seeded from the base-class member tseed, which is left uninitialized whenever the optional 'temp' keyword is not used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_piston_kokkos.cpp:35-41 'FixWallPistonKokkos<DeviceType>::FixWallPistonKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp, int narg, char **arg) : FixWallPiston(lmp, narg, arg), ... rand_pool(tseed + comm->me)'. tseed is declared as a plain int in src/SHOCK/fix_wall_piston.h:40 ('int tempflag, tseed;') and is assigned ONLY inside the 'temp' keyword branch of the base constructor (src/SHOCK/fix_wall_piston.cpp:82-99: 'tseed = utils::inumeric(FLERR,arg[iarg+3],false,lmp);'); the constructor initializes tempflag/roughflag/... at lines 44-55 but never tseed. The CPU style avoids the issue because it only constructs RanMars inside that branch (line 96).
failure_scenario: 'fix p all wall/piston/kk zlo pos 0.0 vel 0.5' (no temp keyword): rand_pool is constructed with an indeterminate seed value; the read of the uninitialized tseed is undefined behaviour and is flagged by valgrind/MemorySanitizer. It also unconditionally allocates a full RNG state pool sized by device concurrency even when no thermostat is requested.
suggested_fix: Initialize tseed (e.g. to 0) in the FixWallPiston constructor next to the other defaults, and/or only construct/seed rand_pool when tempflag is set.

summary: compute_fpair multiplies the LJ derivative by rshift instead of dividing by it, so the pair force is wrong by a factor rshift^2 -- faithfully copied from the CPU style, which has the same expression (pre-existing upstream defect, not a port regression).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_sphere_kokkos.cpp:154 `return r6inv*(lj1*r6inv - lj2) * rshift / r;` mirrors src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_expand_sphere.cpp:61 `fpair = factor_lj * forcelj * rshift / r;` (and single() at the same file). With lj1 = 48*eps*sigma^12 and lj2 = 24*eps*sigma^6 (init_one), forcelj = r6inv*(lj1*r6inv-lj2) equals rshift * (-dE/drshift), so the scalar multiplying del must be forcelj/(rshift*r) -- which is exactly what the sibling style src/pair_lj_expand.cpp:? does: `fpair = factor_lj * forcelj / rshift / r;` (and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_kokkos.cpp:158 `return forcelj/rshift/r;`).
failure_scenario: pair_style lj/expand/sphere (with or without /kk): the force on every pair is scaled by rshift^2 relative to the analytic gradient of the tallied energy, so forces do not match the energy and energy is not conserved; the discrepancy vanishes only at rshift = 1.
suggested_fix: If confirmed upstream, change both the CPU style and the Kokkos kernel to `forcelj / rshift / r` (matching lj/expand); the YAML reference fixtures were generated from the current code, so they must be regenerated together with the fix.
